Everything in the package operates on a `Population` of `Individual`s. An individual
holds four things:

| field | meaning |
|:--|:--|
| `id` | an integer or string label |
| `x` | the covariates, a vector (static over time) |
| `t`, `y` | observation times and observed values |
| `callback` | the *dosing events*, an ODE-solver callback |

The first three are plain arrays. The interesting one is the callback, so this tutorial
starts there and then builds populations from the two datasets in the repository's
`data/` folder, which have very different dosing designs.

```{julia}
using DeepCompartmentModels
using DataFrames, CSV
using CairoMakie

datadir = joinpath(@__DIR__, "..", "data")
nothing # hide
```

## Dosing callbacks

Drug enters the ODE system as an *infusion rate* `I`, which is the last element of the
parameter vector the ODE function receives (this is why the built-in ODEs unpack
`..., I = p`). A dose of `amt` given over `duration` is the rate `amt / duration`
during the infusion and `0` otherwise. `generate_dosing_callback` turns a table of dosing
events into a callback that switches that rate on and off at the right times.

Each row of the table is one dose. With two columns, `[time amount]`, every dose is a
bolus, modelled as a very short infusion (by default one minute, with times in hours).
With four columns, `[time amount rate duration]`, the infusion is given explicitly.

```{julia}
bolus = generate_dosing_callback([0.0 100.0])
infusion = generate_dosing_callback([0.0 100.0 50.0 2.0])      # 100 mg at 50 mg/h for 2 h
repeated = generate_dosing_callback([0.0 100.0; 12.0 100.0; 24.0 100.0])   # three boluses
nothing # hide
```

To see what a callback does we can solve a one-compartment model for a given individual.
`solve(model, individual, z)` takes the ODE parameters `z` (here `[CL, V]`):

```{julia}
model = DCM(one_comp!, 1, Lux.Dense(1 => 2))   # the network is not used when we pass z ourselves
z = Float32[5, 30]                              # CL = 5 L/h, V = 30 L
grid = Float32.(0:0.1:36)

fig = Figure(size = (800, 280))
for (j, (name, cb)) in enumerate(["bolus" => bolus, "2 h infusion" => infusion, "3 boluses" => repeated])
    indv = Individual(1, [70f0], grid, zeros(Float32, length(grid)), cb)
    sol = solve(model, indv, z; saveat = grid, dt = 0.01f0)
    ax = Axis(fig[1, j]; title = name, xlabel = "Time (h)", ylabel = j == 1 ? "mg/L" : "")
    lines!(ax, grid, Array(sol)[1, :])
end
fig
```

A few more options:

- `generate_dosing_callback(A, T)` creates the callback in number type `T` (the default is
  `Float32`). An `Individual` warns if its callback and data types differ.
- `S1` scales all doses, for example to convert mg into the unit of the ODE state.
- `bolus_duration` sets the length of the pseudo-infusion used for boluses.

```{julia}
generate_dosing_callback([0.0 100.0]; S1 = 1 / 1000)   # doses in mg, state in g
nothing # hide
```

## One bolus per subject: warfarin

The warfarin dataset has the usual NONMEM columns. Dose rows have `MDV = 1`, observation
rows `MDV = 0`, and `DVID` tells the two measured responses apart (1 is the plasma
concentration, 2 a pharmacodynamic effect). We only use the concentrations here.

```{julia}
warfarin = DataFrame(CSV.File(joinpath(datadir, "warfarin.csv")))
select(first(warfarin, 3), :ID, :TIME, :WEIGHT, :AGE, :SEX, :DOSE, :RATE, :DURATION, :DV, :MDV)
```

One individual is one `ID` group. The dose matrix comes from the rows with `MDV == 1`
and the observations from the rows with `MDV == 0`:

```{julia}
function warfarin_individual(g)
    covariates = Float32[g.WEIGHT[1], g.AGE[1], g.SEX[1]]
    doses = Matrix{Float32}(g[g.MDV .== 1, [:TIME, :DOSE, :RATE, :DURATION]])
    obs = g[g.MDV .== 0, :]
    return Individual(g.ID[1], covariates, obs.TIME, obs.DV, generate_dosing_callback(doses))
end

pk = warfarin[warfarin.DVID .== 1, :]
warfarin_pop = Population([warfarin_individual(g) for g in groupby(pk, :ID)])
length(warfarin_pop), get_x(warfarin_pop)[:, 1:3]
```

`get_x(population)` stacks the covariates into a matrix with one column per individual, which is
what the network receives. `get_t` and `get_y` return vectors with the times and observations
of each individual.

## Many infusions per subject: tobramycin

In the tobramycin data every dose is an `EVID = 1` row, patients receive dozens of
doses, and there is no rate column. We assume 30-minute infusions, which is common for
this drug; a dataset with a `RATE` or `DURATION` column would use those instead.

```{julia}
tobramycin = DataFrame(CSV.File(joinpath(datadir, "tobramycin.csv")))
select(tobramycin[tobramycin.ID .== 1, :][[1, 2, 3, 34, 35], :], :ID, :TIME, :CP, :EVID, :DOSE, :WT, :AGE, :SEX, :CLCR)
```

```{julia}
function tobramycin_individual(g; infusion_hours = 0.5f0)
    dose_rows = g[g.EVID .== 1, :]
    doses = Float32[dose_rows.TIME dose_rows.DOSE dose_rows.DOSE ./ infusion_hours fill(infusion_hours, nrow(dose_rows))]
    obs = g[g.EVID .== 0, :]
    covariates = Float32[g.WT[1], g.AGE[1], g.SEX[1], g.CLCR[1]]
    return Individual(g.ID[1], covariates, obs.TIME, obs.CP, generate_dosing_callback(doses))
end

tobramycin_pop = Population([tobramycin_individual(g) for g in groupby(tobramycin, :ID)])
length(tobramycin_pop), sum(length.(get_y(tobramycin_pop)))
```

Predicting for one patient with a typical parameter set shows the accumulation over
the repeated infusions:

```{julia}
tobra_model = DCM(one_comp!, 1, Lux.Dense(1 => 2))
indv = tobramycin_pop[1]
grid = Float32.(range(0, maximum(get_t(indv)); length = 600))
sol = solve(tobra_model, indv, Float32[3.5, 20]; saveat = grid, dt = 0.01f0)    # CL = 3.5 L/h, V = 20 L

fig = Figure(size = (800, 300))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1]; xlabel = "Time (h)", ylabel = "Tobramycin (mg/L)")
lines!(ax, grid, Array(sol)[1, :])
scatter!(ax, get_t(indv), get_y(indv); color = :black)
fig
```

::: {.callout-note}
Data types must match: `Population` requires all individuals to have the same concrete
type, which means the same number type, id type and callback type. Building every
individual with the same helper function, as above, takes care of that.
:::

## Checklist

- Dose and observation rows are separated (`MDV` or `EVID`), and observations that are
  `missing` are dropped.
- Times are in the same unit as the ODE's rate constants (hours throughout these tutorials).
- Doses are in the unit of the ODE state. Use `S1` or convert them yourself.
- Covariates are numeric. Categorical ones such as `SEX` need to be encoded first.
- Covariates are a fixed vector per individual. A different covariate per time point
  needs a `TimeVariableIndividual`, see [Status and limitations](../limitations.md).
